notesStmt.note: Whitman planned to write an essay about Elias Hicks for many years. While finishing preparations for the printing of November Boughs, Whitman told Horace Traubel, "Some of these bits were written as many as thirty years ago. Some of them I have written within the past year. They are a miscellaneous lot but they all belong in the same stream" (see Traubel, With Walt Whitman in Camden, 2:42). It is therefore difficult to determine the exact date of the present manuscript. The paper and handwriting suggests that the bulk of the manuscript was written in the 1870s, although the note at the top in red ink appears to have been added later, likely in the late 1880s.

A one-page draft fragment, heavily revised, related to the "George Fox (and Shakspere)" section of Whitman's 1888 essay "Notes (such as they are) founded on Elias Hicks," first published in November Boughs (1888) and later reprinted in Complete Prose Works (1892).
